title: What is Semantic Segmentation
text: Semantic Segmentation means labeling every pixel of an object in an image.
notes:
QUESTION 1: When the car is upside down in the air, can a person react fast enough? (No. Things happen in fractions of a second, so the car's computer must control the thrusters.)
QUESTION 2: Automated or autonomous? (Good discussion! The stunt is planned and practised in a closed area: the computer follows a plan and keeps the car balanced, which is mostly AUTOMATED. AUTONOMOUS would mean deciding by itself in new, busy places, like a city. The engineer says it cannot do that.)
QUESTION 3: Is it ready for the road? (No. Maybe production in 2028, and it must pass safety rules. Exciting videos are not the same as a finished product: always check the facts, as we learned in Part 4.)
INTERPRETER: thrusters = small jets that push the car; production = when the company starts making and selling it.
Source: NBC Nightly News report, supplied by the course organisers. Keep it for classroom use only.

title: Front mode : if there is an existing shape, draw on top of that shape.
text: Front mode : if there is an existing shape, draw on top of that shape.
Rear mode : if there is an existing shape, draw behind that existing shape
Note : if there is no shape drawn in that region then your mode can either be in front mode or rear mode.
Note:  you can leave it rear mode, so that every shape can just fall behind the other.

title: Purpose of the project
text: All people in the image are labeling targets

title: 1. Bounding Box: Face= The person’s head, face, and neck must be contained within the bounding box area.
text: 1. Bounding Box: Face= The person’s head, face, and neck must be contained within the bounding box area.
Hair, hats, headbands, bag, etc. are not include in the bounding box area.
Please note that neck, face until forehead is labeling area to b-box.

title: Labeling target
text: 2. Attributes: Gender, Age, and Image brightness= Please select the correct age, gender, and image brightness seen in the image.

title: Labeling target
text: 3. Polygon: Body= The person’s whole-body outline must be labeled with the polygon tool.
Hair, bags, hat, headbands, etc are labeling target for the body class.

title: Introduction to three-dimensional space and the Principles of LiDAR
text: Introduction to three-dimensional space and the Principles of LiDAR

title: 3D (3-dimensional): Real-world objects exist in 3D space, allowing for deeper perception by using height, width, and depth.
text: 3D (3-dimensional): Real-world objects exist in 3D space, allowing for deeper perception by using height, width, and depth.

title: Spatial coordinates use X, Y, and Z axes to locate points in 3D space.
text: Spatial coordinates use X, Y, and Z axes to locate points in 3D space.
The x-coordinate represents the horizontal position (left or right).
The y-coordinate represents the vertical position (up or down).
The z-coordinate represents the depth or position along the third dimension.
Basics of spatial coordinates and dimensions

title: Dimensions add depth to objects, enhancing realism.
text: Dimensions add depth to objects, enhancing realism.
Spatial coordinates are vital for computer graphics, virtual reality, and simulation.
They enable the creation of realistic 3D environments, immersive experiences, and accurate simulations.
Uses of spatial coordinates and dimensions

title: Navigation and Mapping:
text: Spatial coordinates enable accurate navigation and mapping
Uses of spatial coordinates and dimensions

title: A remote sensing technology
text: Uses laser pulses to measure distances to objects or surfaces.
It creates detailed 3D maps for various applications

title: Autonomous Vehicles (AVs): Object Detection and Map Generation
text: Autonomous Vehicles (AVs): Object Detection and Map Generation
Aerial Surveying: Accurately map terrain, forests, and cities.
Geographic Information Systems (GIS): Maps for urban planning and environmental management.
Archeology: LiDAR uncovers hidden archaeological sites by scanning terrain with precision.
Forestry Monitoring: LiDAR measures tree heights and monitors forest health.
Disaster Management: LiDAR maps disaster areas to aid rescue operations and assess damage.

title: Conclusion
text: In conclusion, 3D and LiDAR systems collectively revolutionize our interaction with the digital and physical worlds.
The precision and speed of LiDAR contribute significantly to the depth and accuracy of 3D perception, impacting a wide range of applications and industries.

title: PCD is termed Point Cloud Data. These are points that represent data picked up by a LiDAR signal.
text: PCD is termed Point Cloud Data. These are points that represent data picked up by a LiDAR signal.

title: Why does this PCD Project exist?
text: Why does this PCD Project exist?
notes:
Accurate Object Detection and Recognition: Autonomous vehicles need to detect and recognize various objects in their environment, such as pedestrians, vehicles, cyclists, and obstacles.
Depth Perception and Spatial Awareness: This allows autonomous vehicles to perceive the distance to objects, which is crucial for making safe driving decisions such as braking, lane changes, and avoiding collisions.

title: Why does this PCD Project exist?
text: Why does this PCD Project exist?
notes:
Environment Understanding: 3D PCD labelling helps in understanding the layout of the environment, including road boundaries, lane markings, traffic signs, and other infrastructure elements.
Enhanced Safety and Reliability: Accurate 3D PCD labelling improves the safety and reliability of autonomous vehicles by reducing the risk of misinterpreting the surroundings.
